title: ci: split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache & parallelism
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows have grown slow and brittle as we added more job matrices and release steps. This increases iteration time for engineers and wastes CI minutes. This PR splits the previous single workflows into separate, focused workflows for lint, unit/integration tests, and release automation, and introduces improved cache keys + controlled parallelism to reduce redundant work.

Summary of changes: split .github/workflows/ci.yml into .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, and .github/workflows/release.yml; extract reusable cache and matrix logic into .github/actions/cache-utils; tighten cache keys to include os/hash of lockfiles and test seed; introduce job-level parallelism controls (max-parallel) for expensive matrix runs; consolidate and prune deprecated actions (old/setup-node v1 -> actions/setup-node v4); add documentation and an opt-in canary for release automation.

Testing and rollout: CI was iterated on in this branch; lint and test workflows were validated across matrix nodes and platforms. Release workflow was exercised against the internal canary channel (dry-run and simulated tag). We’ll roll this across repos by enabling the new workflows and deprecating the old combined workflow next week.

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and add new files
- [x] Add shared cache/action utilities
- [x] Validate lint and test matrices on linux/mac/windows
- [x] Run release dry-run on canary channel
- [x] Update docs/tools/ci/README.md

Notes: This is non-breaking for developers. The release workflow includes a short probation period where publish is gated behind an approved dry-run. Further follow-ups (ENG-2401) will tune matrix footprints and add cross-repo templates for standardization.
